subject: SLO qualification scope & proposed benchmark test plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: SLO qualification scope & proposed benchmark test plan

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. This focuses on the performance/SLO checks we discussed (latency, throughput, concurrency, streaming behavior) and the minimal reproducibility artifacts we need to run a deterministic qualification.

Summary of goals we aligned on:
- Latency SLOs: p50 <= 120 ms, p95 <= 350 ms for 16-token generation (server-side streaming enabled).
- Throughput target: sustained 45 requests/sec steady-state at 4 concurrent clients (burst to 150rps allowed for short spikes).
- Concurrency: validate up to 60 simultaneous open streams (long-poll streaming sessions with partial tokens).
- Streaming: support partial-token flush every 50ms, client receives chunked events; verify reassembly under varying network RTT (50ms/100ms).

Proposed benchmark methodology (high level):
1) Prompt sets: we will use a mixed-case prompt bundle (attached: benchmark_prompt_set_v2.csv) that reflects 60/30/10 split of short/medium/long prompts (10–16 tokens / 32–64 / 128+).
2) Harness: Redwood will run the perf harness (perf_harness_runbook.md attached) against your test VPC or a Redwood dedicated sandbox — we need to confirm which environment you prefer.
3) Measurement definitions: latency measured end-to-end (API request -> final token delivered); p95/p99 computed over 10k steady-state requests per test; throughput measured as successful responses/sec excluding warmup.
4) Repro rules: fixed RNG seed, cold-start warmup window (2 minutes), KV cache disabled for the canonical reproducibility run, and model weights pinned to the test commit (we'll provide the hash).

Open asks / next steps for Acme:
- Confirm environment: do you want Redwood to execute the harness from our dedicated sandbox, or will you provide temporary AWS creds for an in-VPC run?
- Provide representative traffic profile (sample attached is fine if it matches).
- Confirm which model variant to qualify (suggestion: redwood-1-large-quant or open-evo-3b for comparison).

Attachments: [attachment: benchmark_prompt_set_v2.csv (csv)], [attachment: perf_harness_runbook.md (md)], [attachment: sample_traffic_profile.json (json)]

I assigned Rishi to own the tech coordination; he'll follow up with specific run configs. If that all looks good, can we lock a 2-hour window next Tues or Wed (your timezone) to run the baseline qualification?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Vanessa — this is very clear and helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Environment: procurement prefers that Redwood run initial discovery from your sandbox (faster), then we’ll validate the canonical run inside our VPC with short-lived creds. Is that workflow OK?

2) Traffic profile: the sample you attached looks close; our peak traffic shape is slightly different — ~70% short prompts, 25% medium, 5% very long. I attached a small sample payload (we'll send a larger anonymized dump by EOD).

3) Model: prefer to validate against both redwood-1-large-quant and an internal tuned variant (we can provide a containerized model for in-VPC runs). Will Redwood's harness accept a custom model artifact for the in-VPC step, or do we need to run that locally and share logs?

4) Timing: Tuesday afternoon PT works for us (2–4pm PT).

On the reproducibility items: can you confirm what exactly you mean by 'disable KV cache' — do you expect top-level cache flags off, or no prefix caching at runtime? We want to make sure our application-level cache doesn't get disabled inadvertently.

Hey team — quick technical clarifications and constraints from the Redwood side: 

- Environment/workflow: sandbox run from our side is fine for initial profiling. For the canonical, in-VPC run we can accept an AMI/container or run directly against your endpoint with short-lived IAM creds. If you provide the model artifact, we'll mount it in our runner and run the same harness for parity.

- KV cache: by "disable KV cache" we mean disable server-side KV LRU that would persist cross-requests for the canonical reproducible run. Application-level prefix caching (client side) is OK to keep, but please note we will document any client-side caching in the run metadata. For the canonical reproducible baseline we prefer no server-side caching so results are deterministic.

- Measurement config (I will attach the run JSON to the Drive link):
  * Warmup: 2 minutes at 30% target load.
  * Steady window: 10,000 requests across 10 minutes.
  * Latency: measure from request start -> last token flush (for streaming runs we mark completion on final chunk).
  * Concurrency shaping: use 4 client threads, ramp linearly to 60 open streams to validate behavior under heavy multiplexing.
  * Network simulation: optional in-sandbox step with 50ms/100ms RTT box to capture tail behavior (we can simulate via tc).

- Model pinning: send us the model commit hash (or container digest). We'll pin the run to that digest. For quantized variants we note quantization bits and kernel selection.

I put the perf runbook and the example harness config in the shared Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/perf-harness-v2 — please add your sample dump there so we can stage the tests.

Proposed next step: confirm Tue 2027-12-07 14:00–16:00 PT for sandbox run. I'll pre-provision the runner and drop the precise run command in the Drive folder (and post a HubSpot note: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2027-Q4-42).
